intent: Specify the public selection function `order_stat::quickselect::select(x: &mut [T], k: usize)` instantiated at `T = i32`. In Lean it is `quickselect.select core.I32.Insts.CoreCmpOrd x k` with `x : Slice Std.I32`, `k : Std.Usize`; the `&mut` slice is threaded functionally, i.e. the call returns the final contents of `x`.

manual_mutants.note: right-hand recursion uses k - pivot instead of k - pivot - 1 (off by one)
when k lands exactly on the pivot the unpartitioned slice is returned
small-slice sort never compares against the last element
manual_mutants.after: let i2 ← (do let n ← core.slice.Slice.len x; n - 1#usize)

manual_mutants.note: partition forgets to move the pivot into its final position
manual_mutants.before: let x2 ← core.slice.Slice.swap x1 store i1

manual_mutants.note: small-slice (len < 5) sort compares in the wrong direction (sorts descending)
partition moves elements greater than the pivot to the left
partition overwrites x[store] with the pivot instead of swapping: still partitioned, but an element is lost and the pivot duplicated
manual_mutants.before: let x2 ← core.slice.Slice.swap x1 store i1
manual_mutants.after: let x2 ← (do let p ← Slice.index_usize x1 i1; Slice.update x1 store p)

manual_mutants.note: small-slice sort copies the smaller element instead of swapping: output sorted but not a permutation of the input
manual_mutants.before: then let x1 ← core.slice.Slice.swap x i j
manual_mutants.after: then let x1 ← (do let t ← Slice.index_usize x j; Slice.update x i t)
